subject.title: [Bug]: Teams Graph/media guarded fetches reject RFC2544-proxied hosts

question: Is the hostname-scoped RFC2544 exception proposed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107164 an acceptable Teams SSRF boundary, and what proof is required before it may merge?
rationale: Allowing an otherwise blocked address range is intentional security policy, and source inspection alone cannot decide the repository's acceptable residual risk or live-proof threshold.

options.title: Require live proxy proof
options.body: Verify Graph and media requests through an RFC2544 fake-IP proxy while demonstrating that non-allowlisted hosts remain blocked before merging.

options.title: Accept focused policy tests
options.body: Merge using the host-scoping and negative unit coverage if maintainers judge the policy construction sufficient without a live Teams environment.

options.title: Retain strict blocking
options.body: Decline the exception and document that RFC2544 fake-IP proxy deployments are unsupported for Teams guarded fetches.

recommendation.title: Require live proxy proof
recommendation.body: Verify Graph and media requests through an RFC2544 fake-IP proxy while demonstrating that non-allowlisted hosts remain blocked before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person most directly to both the Teams Graph implementation and its SSRF runtime seam.
